findings.reason: the plan must extend `_store._write_through_sibling_temporary` to carry binary payloads (a mode/type keyword) or name these sites as retained exceptions, otherwise §9's "every file-write site becomes a call to the promoted primitive" is unachievable and the binary sites fork a second writer.
findings.text: §9 routes the two byte-writing asset publishers (`reckon/serve.py:498-503` writes `response.read()` bytes, `:562-567` writes `.encode()` bytes) and the byte thumbnail cache (`:2320-2323`, `write_bytes`) onto the promoted primitive "with its payload as the render callback", but that primitive opens its handle in text mode and types its callback as `Callable[[TextIO], None]` (`reckon/_store.py:409`), so a bytes payload cannot pass; `reckon/ledger.py:1032-1037` (sqlite rebuild) fails the same way

findings.reason: the section must name the one new public symbol (and its relationship to `write_json_atomically`) so the +1 accounting is checkable against `reckon/interface_counts.py` at the merged head.
findings.text: §8 asserts "the public_definitions family grows by exactly one, the promoted primitive", but does not state the promoted primitive's public name, and leaves the already-public `write_json_atomically` (`reckon/_store.py:463`) as a public adapter over it, so the section both fails to name the surface it adds and risks counting two public entry points to one mechanism

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the promoted primitive hides substantial behaviour (unique `O_EXCL` sibling, umask-vs-chmod mode handling, optional fsync, atomic rename, optional directory fsync) behind one render-callback function (`reckon/_store.py:419-460`); §8 adds no scatter of shallow wrappers and §9 adds one function, so the design concentrates depth rather than spreading it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9 directs every file-write site onto the promoted `_store._write_through_sibling_temporary`, whose interface is text-only (`os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8")` at `reckon/_store.py:409`, `render: Callable[[TextIO], None]`), yet the very sites §9 enumerates in `serve.py` and `ledger.py` carry bytes, so the design will fork a second bytes path instead of extending the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 adds one public definition and states why the family cannot shrink (the retired forks are private and uncounted), and §7 adds none, but §8's claim that the promoted primitive grows the family "by exactly one" is unsupported by the plan's own text, which never names the new public name and leaves the pre-existing public adapter `write_json_atomically` (`reckon/_store.py:463`) beside it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the exact existing machinery by file and symbol before proposing anything: §8 cites `reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary` (verified at `reckon/_store.py:419`, with `write_json_atomically` a thin adapter over it at `:511`), §9 cites `reckon/interface_counts.py:read_trees`/`definitions` (`:326`,`:76`), explicitly rejects `reckon/clones.py:functions_in` with a reason ("returns token windows and holds no call"), and quotes the census predicate — which I opened and confirmed at `docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:262-274`, nested under the JSON-encoding branch exactly as §9 states.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 states in its own text that "the repair extends the owner rather than adding beside it", and §9 states "No new function is added to any migrating module" with the private helpers deleted; a site that needs a missing behaviour is directed to extend the primitive once rather than wrap it.
